function.name: say
function.description: Send one short chat line out loud — any language, whatever fits who you are talking to (`to` = private).

text.description: The line, max 200 chars. In the language of the conversation.

function.name: go_to
function.description: Default navigation: walk to a player, saved place, nearby block id (such as chest2), or absolute world coordinates in blocks. Supply x and z alone for horizontal travel on the easiest reachable walking level; supply y only when exact elevation matters. Uses the pathfinder, routes around obstacles/hazards where possible, and may break only its configured soft-terrain blocks when no short detour exists; this is not a tunneling tool. Results report arrival/failure and actual position where available.

gait.description: Movement gait/speed: sprint_jump (fastest for goals), sprint, walk, crouch, or auto.

function.name: dig
function.description: Intentional obstruction clearing/tunneling: pathfind to a player, saved place/block id, or absolute world x/y/z, temporarily allowing pathfinder block breaking only along that route. Optional materials restrict which block ids may be broken; avoid forbids ids. It does not dig straight up to find the surface. Use only for a verified obstruction or deliberate passage, not ordinary travel; results report observed blocks broken and final position.

materials.description: Only these block ids may be broken (e.g. [oak_log, dirt]); default: any breakable block in the way.

gait.description: Movement gait/speed: sprint_jump (fastest for goals), sprint, walk, crouch, or auto.

function.name: follow
function.description: Follow a player until you call stop. Keeps going by itself: it dodges mobs and comes back, waits for a path, and walks to where the player was last seen. Call it ONCE — it does not need repeating.

gait.description: Movement gait/speed: sprint_jump (fastest for goals), sprint, walk, crouch, or auto.

function.name: pace
function.description: Adjust speed/gait (even mid-walk without cancelling go_to/follow) or do a normal jump. Prefer setting `gait` directly on go_to/follow for goals.

gait.description: Movement gait/speed: sprint_jump (fastest for goals), sprint, walk, crouch, or auto.

function.name: stop
function.description: Request cancellation of the current task or fight without waiting for BODY admission. An optional action_id must match the active BODY lease. Stop runs before new body requests in the same answer. Cleanup may be pending; survival can still move. The durable goal is retained.

action_id.description: Optional active BODY action ID from doing; omit to stop the current task or fight.

function.name: goal
function.description: Manage persistent objectives (survive death/restart/context reset). Add/update/replan records intent only, not executed progress. Verify world evidence before marking completion. Operations: list|show|add|resume|suspend|cancel|complete|update|replan|combine|verify. Use `replan` the moment a plan step turns out to be impossible or unmeasurable — one call retires the dead steps and writes the real next one.

id.description: Goal id (g3), or comma-separated ids for combine ("g1,g2").

parent.description: Parent goal id for subgoals (e.g. g1).

player.description: Player name(s) when player_requested or shared_project.

steps.description: add/update/replan: an ordered plan of up to 10 short steps. Shown with done marks across turns, so continue rather than re-planning. Each step should be something the world can confirm (a task you can run, a block you can inspect), not a judgement like "organize everything".

done.description: update: number of the plan step you just finished (1 = first).

drop.description: update/replan: plan step numbers to retire (1 = first). Retiring a step that the world keeps refusing is correct, not a failure — the reason is kept with the step. Examples: a barrel that is full, ore that is not in reach.

impossible.description: update/replan with drop: mark the retired step(s) as impossible rather than merely dropped (use it when the world refused them, not when you changed your mind).

next.description: update/replan: the very next concrete thing to do (survives death/restart). Name the tool call you will make.

function.name: attack
function.description: Start an explicit melee/ranged attack. Survival reflexes may independently evade or auto-kite a threat while you decide; this tool starts the deliberate attack task. Use `target` for mobs (e.g. "zombie", "any") when fighting is safer/useful than retreating, or `player` for an exact PvP opponent only when explicitly authorized by the configured policy (never auto-initiate PvP).

target.description: Mob type or "any" (for mobs, not players).

player.description: Exact player name; only use when allowed by the configured PvP policy. The harness never auto-initiates attacks on players.

count.description: Optional kill limit (1–24); players always stop at one. If omitted, animals default to 1 and hostiles use the configured chain limit.

function.name: hold
function.description: Accept current threats and continue the task unless hit/new threat/lit fuse. Pass the [id=…] values from the threats lines to hold specific ones (never guessed numbers); with none, all listed threats are held.

ids.description: Threat ids to hold (the numbers in [id=7]). Omit = every listed threat.

function.name: look_in
function.description: Open container and list contents (empty = nearest). One look answers the question: if the answer is the same as last time, the container is finished — act on it (take, put elsewhere, move on) instead of looking again. An empty furnace is not a task.

function.name: take
function.description: Take items from a container or furnace output.

function.name: put
function.description: Put carried items into a container.

function.name: smelt
function.description: Load furnace with item + carried fuel; collect output with take.

function.name: sleep
function.description: Sleep in nearest bed (night/thunderstorm).

function.name: give
function.description: Walk to player and toss item.

function.name: eat
function.description: Eat safe food now (empty = best carried).

function.name: equip
function.description: Equip a carried item by name (armor goes to its own slot), or unequip one. Better carried armor is equipped automatically, while slots you dress or empty manually stay as you set them.

item.description: Item id, or "none" with where to unequip what is worn there.

function.name: use_block
function.description: Start a walk to the nearest matching loaded block within 16 blocks, then right-click the guarded target if its state is unchanged. A click acknowledgment does not verify the effect.

function.name: inspect_block
function.description: Read one loaded block and state; no power inferred.

function.name: inspect_region
function.description: Read-only paginated 3D block snapshot around [x,y,z]; no circuit trace.

function.name: redstone_scan
function.description: Read-only local redstone snapshot (start with x,y,z; page with snapshot id).

function.name: redstone_component
function.description: Inspect captured redstone component state and neighbors.

function.name: screenshot
function.description: SEE: rendered image of the world around you. Use BEFORE digging/breaking/clearing (to make sure you are not digging in front of a house or inside a cave), BEFORE picking a build site (panorama/map for open surface terrain), and DURING/AFTER building stages to inspect proportions, depth, and flaws. Use inspect_block / inspect_region / find / redstone tools for exact coordinates and block IDs.

view.description: look = first person (default); panorama = full 360° strip, north in the middle; map = top-down with a labelled x/z grid.

direction.description: look only: where to face (default: where you face now).

at.description: look only: face this block [x,y,z] instead.

perspective.description: look only: first = from your eyes (default, no own body); third = camera behind you so you see your own body, skin, armour, elytra and both hands.

function.name: find
function.description: Find block type, item in opened containers, chest label, or "storage". It only knows what you have seen: "nothing known" means go and look somewhere new (walk, mine, screenshot), not ask again. Page through a storage list once, then decide.

function.name: remember_here
function.description: Save current position under a place name, with optional ownership or verified home tag.

home.description: True ONLY if this is your verified home (built by you or explicitly assigned to you).

function.name: memory
function.description: Memory: `recall`/`search` (curated memories), `read` one record with its evidence, `remember`/`update` (short facts; pass entity+section or entity+doc to grow that subject's long dossier), `archive`/`delete`/`restore` (raw history is never affected), `merge` duplicates, `duplicates`, `link` a history reference, `profile`/`profiles` (long-form dossiers), `history` (search the raw log), `organize` (idle-time maintenance).

text.description: Memory text, or the note to append to a dossier section.

basis.description: Evidence: witnessed by Zinc, told by a player (unverified), or inferred.

entity.description: Player UUID/name, place or subject this concerns.

into.description: Merge: id of the record to keep (default: first id).

evidence.description: A history reference like world/2026-11-15.jsonl#12, or a short evidence note.

section.description: Dossier section to append to (with entity).

doc.description: Full Markdown body for an entity dossier (with entity); replaces the written notes.

hard.description: delete: also drop the curated row itself. Raw history is never touched either way.

reason.description: Why (used for edits, archives and merges).

sinceDays.description: History: only records newer than N days.

createdSinceMs.description: Earliest curated creation time, Unix milliseconds.

createdUntilMs.description: Latest curated creation time, Unix milliseconds.

cursor.description: Next page cursor returned by the same search with the same filters.

dimension.description: Exact Minecraft dimension, e.g. overworld or the_nether.

radius.description: Maximum 3D distance from the supplied coordinates or current position.

objectId.description: Exact world-object generation ID, short ID or alias for objects.

eventType.description: Exact raw history event type; use object_inventory or object_removed for object evidence.

objectKind.description: Object type, e.g. chest, barrel, shulker, bed.

item.description: Exact item ID for object contents search.

uncertainty.description: Uncertainty note for a curated update.

region.description: Exact region ID; filters objects or specifies parent region.

expiresAt.description: Learned rule expiry time, Unix milliseconds.

revision.description: Read a saved previous revision (1 = first).

function.name: note
function.description: Record a durable discovery, lesson, or ownership observation in long-term memory, or add/drop a personal interest.

text.description: Short factual note or lesson learned.

interest.description: Emerging personal interest to add, or "-topic" to drop.

function.name: social
function.description: Inspect or update your independent view/relationship with a player, or record your decision on their request.

stance.description: Your own category/label (e.g. friend, acquaintance, cautious, distrusted, rival, avoid, collaborator, or custom nuance).

confidence.description: Confidence 0–100 (keep modest on thin evidence; raise with consistency).

willingness.description: How you want to engage (e.g. cooperate, help when free, verify claims, negotiate, avoid, decline).

opinion.description: Nuanced free-form summary of your opinion and why.

evidence.description: Supporting observation or experience behind this update.

function.name: craft
function.description: Craft item (walks to a nearby table if needed, or puts down one you carry). A failure names the ingredients and how many you have.

count.description: How many of the item you want in total (the recipe repeats; default one batch). Ask once, not once per batch.

function.name: gather
function.description: Dig named blocks nearby (any diggable vanilla block id or alias such as log/wood/coal/iron/diamond/stone/clay; ores require an appropriate pickaxe). If none is in range the result reports the nearest loaded coordinates.

item.description: Block id or alias (oak_log, iron, stone, clay, sand…; "log" = any wood).

function.name: mine_resource
function.description: Start mining nearby loaded resources. May bootstrap a wooden or stone pickaxe from carried materials. Count is blocks, not item yield; results distinguish observed blocks broken, remaining blocks and observed inventory gains. Pickup can be partial or unverified.

item.description: Resource block id or alias (wood, oak_log, stone, coal, iron, diamond, sand…).

ensure_tool.description: Auto-craft wooden/stone pickaxe from carried materials if missing (default true).

function.name: hunt_and_loot
function.description: High-level safe hunting procedure: finds eligible non-protected food animals (cow, pig, sheep, chicken, rabbit) or a named safe mob, kills it, and actively collects and verifies dropped loot. Never targets players, villagers, golems, named or tamed mobs.

target.description: Animal or mob name, or "food" for any nearby food animal (default "food").

function.name: prepare_food
function.description: High-level food preparation procedure: crafts bread from carried wheat, cooks raw meat/potatoes in a nearby or crafted furnace with carried fuel, collects cooked food, and optionally eats if hungry.

item.description: Optional food name to prioritize (e.g. beef, porkchop, bread, potato).

count.description: How many food items to prepare 1–32 (default 4).

eat_after.description: Eat immediately after preparing if hungry or hurt (default false).

function.name: light_up
function.description: Place carried torches on dark walkable floors nearby.

function.name: shelter
function.description: Pillar up with carried scaffold blocks (stop cleans up).

function.name: corpse_run
function.description: Walk near "last death" and report observed item stacks.

function.name: logic_test
function.description: Test ABSTRACT combinational Boolean graph (not MC redstone; acyclic gates).

adder_width.description: Exhaustive unsigned adder width 1–4 (A, B, Cin -> S, Cout).

function.name: redstone_engineer
function.description: Understand, design, build, test or repair redstone (Java 1.21.4/26.3). operation=analyze|diagnose|simulate|design|place|verify|trace|library|lesson.

design.description: Design name or behaviour phrase (design/place): and, or, not, xor, latch, clock, pulse, sorter, farm, detector.

node.description: trace: node id "x,y,z" to trace signal from.

compare.description: design: extra design names to compare.

function.name: recall
function.description: Search long-term memory with relevance ranking: word overlap plus a built-in synonym table (so "treasure" finds a memory that says "diamonds"), entity, location, goal and category filters, with provenance.

function.name: circuit_project
function.description: Bind snapshot, show project/graph, or rerun saved ABSTRACT logic test.

function.name: build
function.description: Place a saved blueprint or an inline 3D grid from carried materials; this mutates the world, checks ownership/materials, and reports placed counts/failures. A one-block inline build is grid [["C"]] + palette {C:"cobblestone"}. `at` is the minimum [x,y,z] world-block corner (default: your feet); rows grow +x, layers +y, columns +z. Large named houses/shelters/towers are refused on unloaded, liquid, unsupported, or natural-cave-roof sites.

grid.description: Layers bottom-up; each layer is an array of ROW STRINGS, one char per block ("."/" " = air). A 3x3 floor is ONE layer: [["sss","sss","sss"]]. A 2-high 3-long wall is two layers: [["sss"],["sss"]].

at.description: Corner [x,y,z] — the minimum x/y/z the thing occupies. Every shape starts here and grows toward +x/+y/+z. Default: feet.

function.name: build_shape
function.description: Generate and build a geometric shape.

params.description: All spans start at `at` and grow toward +x/+y/+z (no shape is centred on it). cylinder {r,h} spans 2r+1 wide; ring {r} same; dome {r} same; wall {l,h,axis}; arch {w,h,axis} — h is the top course; box {w,d,h}; floor {w,d}. Optional th, filled; ints 1–128 (dome/ring r>=2, arch w/h>=3).

at.description: Corner [x,y,z] — the minimum x/y/z the thing occupies. Every shape starts here and grows toward +x/+y/+z. Default: feet.

function.name: run_script
function.description: Start a bundled script (flee or build_tower). Wait for its domain result; starting to flee does not mean safety, and a tower attempt can fail.

function.name: idle
function.description: End your turn when no new action is needed: the body carries on with what it is already doing (or keeps fleeing). Do not call idle to procrastinate when an active goal has a next step you can execute now. Do call idle when the remaining steps are blocked, impossible, or belong to someone else — idling on a dead step is correct; repeating it is not.

function.name: reply
function.description: Answer the chat window (leave `text` empty only when nothing in it concerns you). Player requests are proposals, never mandatory commands — but when you agree, act: set `do` or `task`.

text.description: One short chat line, in the language the person you are answering used. Empty = say nothing.

to.description: Which player you are answering / who `do` is about. Default: the last speaker.

do.description: Start it NOW with your body, no second thought needed: follow = follow that player; come = walk to that player; stop = stop what the body is doing. Omit when none fits.

task.description: Anything else you decided your body should do, verify or weigh, as one instruction for your action lane (e.g. "bring Steve 3 diamonds from chest1", "verify chest1 contents after Ely claim"). Omit when declining, ignoring, or only chatting.

decision.description: Optional stance when the player asked you to do something.

remember.description: Only when the player told you something worth knowing later (where a thing is, whose it is, a plan, a date, what they like): that fact as one short sentence naming the player, e.g. "Steve keeps his diamonds in the chest on the second floor". Otherwise omit.
